title: Ann Connor — the ministers of Bethel, and George Marshall
subtitle: Bethel Presbyterian Church, Historical Room — a talk in the room, date unknown
date_source: Searched and found no date: the filed transcript end to end, the .srt, the transcription JSON (date_recorded: 'UNKNOWN (not stated on the tape; c. 2001 assumed by the archive)'), the notes, and the filename. The tape states no date, names no anniversary, and refers to no datable outside event; the archive README's row for this item also records UNKNOWN. The archive's working assumption is c. 2001 — John Decker's, on the grounds that it is the same era and the same speaker as the Ann Connor Sides A and B cassettes, which date themselves by the 225th anniversary (1776 + 225). That is an assumption and is recorded as one, never as evidence. The 14 May 1851 letter read on the tape is period content, not a date for the recording.

provenance.collection: Bethel Presbyterian Church — Historical Room oral histories
provenance.capture_notes: One continuous room recording, ALAC 48 kHz stereo 16-bit, 1,904.213 s (31 m 44 s), 75,371,783 bytes, sha256 recomputed here; the source JSON records md5 198d5633a0dc95e812faaf8488d83fe4. Measured on the master as received: mean -31.2 dBFS, peak -3.4 dBFS, even across the file. Speech runs 0:09.6 to 30:50.3 per the timed cues; the final 49 s from 1,855 s measures RMS -66.2 dBFS, peak -37.2 dBFS, so it is room tone. (The source notes print 31:50.3, which lies beyond the end of the 1,904.2 s file and is a typo; the .srt's last cue is 30:50.110.) A mono 64 kbps transfer copy, 1,852.0 s, sits beside the master; it is the master with the silent tail cut and nothing inside the talk touched.

speakers.label: ANN
speakers.name: Ann Connor
speakers.note: Per the archive: the tape never states her name. She is the same speaker as the Ann Connor Sides A and B cassettes in this collection. The label is ANN because the tape gives no fuller name.

speakers.label: AUDIENCE
speakers.name: unidentified audience member
speakers.note: One turn only, at 29:58 ('Of course, maybe they were hauling it 50 miles'), answered by Ann. Attribution is by dialogue structure, not by voice: a pitch comparison put the objection at 186 Hz against Ann's 205-216 Hz, a margin inside her own range across the recording, so pitch does not settle it.
